subject: physiology
title: Cerebellum and basal ganglia function

steps.tx: The **cerebellum** rules trunk and gait from the vermis and limb coordination from the hemispheres, with Purkinje cells as sole inhibitory cortical output, climbing fibres teaching by errors and mossy fibres carrying context. Ataxia widens the base with falls, intention tremor overshoots, and gaze evoked nystagmus appears, tested by finger nose past pointing, heel shin sliding, rapid alternating failure in dysdiadochokinesia, and Romberg splitting proprioception loss. Alcohol shrinks the anterior vermis toward a stooping gait.
steps.say: Midline vermis steadies the trunk and gait, each hemisphere fine tunes the same side limbs, and Purkinje cells provide the only cortical output, all inhibitory, as the circuit diagram shows. Mossy fibres bring context, climbing fibres report errors, and failure gives wide based ataxia with intention tremor. Finger nose, heel shin and rapid alternating movements expose limb incoordination, while chronic alcohol use shrivels the front vermis.

vis.alt: Circuit of the cerebellar cortex: cortex through pontine nuclei sends mossy fibres to granule cells, parallel fibres excite Purkinje cells; climbing fibres from the inferior olive also excite Purkinje cells; Purkinje cells inhibit deep cerebellar nuclei, the only output.
vis.caption: Purkinje cells are the sole cortical output and are inhibitory; mossy fibres carry context, climbing fibres carry errors.

steps.tx: The **basal ganglia** take cortical input at striatum of caudate and putamen: the direct D1 pathway disinhibits movement as go, the indirect D2 pathway brakes as no go, dopamine from nigra modulates both, GABA hushes every output, and thalamus returns the result to cortex. Too little braking dances as hyperkinetic, too much braking freezes as hypokinetic, across motor putamen loops for action, associative caudate loops for planning, and limbic accumbens loops for reward, unlocked by subthalamic deep brain stimulation.
steps.say: Cortex excites the striatum, then two routes compete: the direct route frees the thalamus to allow movement, the indirect route tightens pallidal braking, and dopamine from the substantia nigra tips the balance toward action, wired in the pathways diagram. Motor loops through putamen are moving limbs, caudate loops are planning, and accumbens loops are weighing reward. Too little braking produces dancing movements, too much produces freezing, and subthalamic stimulation can rebalance severe disease.

vis.alt: Wiring diagram of the basal ganglia. Cortex excites striatum. Direct pathway: striatum D1 inhibits GPi, which frees the thalamus to excite cortex. Indirect pathway: striatum D2 inhibits GPe, which frees the subthalamic nucleus to excite GPi, which inhibits thalamus. Substantia nigra pars compacta dopamine excites D1 cells and inhibits D2 cells.
vis.caption: Direct pathway releases movement; indirect pathway brakes it; dopamine pushes toward movement.

steps.tx: **Parkinson disease** spells TRAP as rest tremor, rigidity, akinesia and postural instability, with pill rolling asymmetric tremor, Lewy body death in nigra, levodopa as gold standard that wears off into peak dose dyskinesia, freezing at doorways, selegiline sparing by MAO-B, and pramipexole risking gambling impulses. Mimics stiffen differently: progressive supranuclear palsy falls with vertical gaze failure, multiple system atrophy adds autonomic failure and stridor, corticobasal degeneration alienates a limb, and dementia with Lewy bodies fluctuates with visuals, while cueing physiotherapy frees steps.
steps.say: Rest tremor that rolls pills, stiffness, slowness and postural instability spell Parkinson disease from nigral dopamine loss, the circuit redrawn in the figure. Levodopa remains the best treatment but wears off and can overshoot into dyskinesia, and freezing traps patients at doorways until visual cues free them. Lookalikes separate by early falls with gaze palsy, autonomic failure with stridor, an alien limb, or fluctuating visual hallucinations.

vis.alt: Parkinson disease circuit: loss of substantia nigra dopamine weakens the direct pathway and releases the indirect pathway, so globus pallidus internus over-inhibits the thalamus, causing bradykinesia, rigidity and rest tremor.
vis.caption: TRAP: Tremor at rest, Rigidity, Akinesia, Postural instability; the cause is nigral dopamine loss.

steps.tx: **Chorea** dances in Huntington disease as CAG repeats anticipate with psychiatric change, flings in hemiballismus from a subthalamic stroke, follows streptococci in Sydenham chorea of girls, deposits copper in Wilson disease with Kayser Fleischer rings needing chelation, and chews in tardive dyskinesia after dopamine blockers, depleted by tetrabenazine at depression cost. Predictive genetic counselling guards Huntington families, juvenile disease stiffens as Westphal variant, dystonia twists into torticollis eased by botulinum or task cramps in writers, and Tourette tics suppress briefly.
steps.say: Too little braking releases unwanted movement: Huntington disease wastes caudate under an expanding CAG repeat, a subthalamic stroke flings the opposite limbs, and post streptococcal Sydenham chorea affects schoolgirls, all listed in the causes table. Wilson disease loads basal ganglia with copper ringed at the cornea, dopamine blockers leave tardive chewing, and tetrabenazine quiets chorea at a mood price. Dystonic twisting and suppressible tics complete the hyperkinetic family.

vis.alt: Table of hyperkinetic movement disorders by lesion: Huntington caudate and putamen with CAG repeat, hemiballismus contralateral subthalamic nucleus, Sydenham chorea after streptococcal infection, Wilson disease copper in basal ganglia, tardive dyskinesia from dopamine blockers.
vis.caption: Hemiballismus: subthalamic nucleus stroke. Huntington: caudate loss and CAG expansion.
